text:
Maria: Hey, ran a long-run profile on the KV cache with a 12k token trace and I'm seeing steady memory growth on Hosted but not on Dedicated. Growth ~+10–15MB/min after warmup. anyone else?
Akash: interesting — do you have pmap/rss samples? Could be fragmentation or page churn.
Maria: pasted main snippet from pmap + jemalloc stats: 
```
RSS: 34G -> 36.2G over 90min
jemalloc: allocated 32.8G active 33.9G mapped 36.1G
kv_pages_in_use: 1.1M -> 1.3M
page-frag-estimate: ~8% -> 18%
```
Priya: Host stack uses kernel 5.10 + older nvidia driver in our hosted pool, Dedicated is on 6.1 + newer driver. Could be userfaultfd / pagefault path differences.
Jonas: Also check MTU + VXLAN overhead on Hosted VPC — we saw bad reassembly causing additional copies that blow apart contiguous allocations.
Maria: I toggled scatter-gather on the runtime and retested. With SG off growth stopped but latency increased 4–6ms. Means we might be double-copying during network recv leading to fragmentation.
Theo: Any kernel selection differences in the runtime? We pick kernels based on seq-len percentiles; maybe Hosted fallback logic uses different kernels that allocate different slab sizes.
Akash: Good point. On Dedicated we use "kv-v2-compact" kernel path for >1024 seqs, Hosted is falling back to "kv-v1-std" more often because of older cuda/cuBLAS behavior. Those kernels have different KV page pitch.
Priya: If the page pitch differs, jemalloc arena fragmentation will differ. Can you dump /proc/<pid>/smaps and the runtime's page-chunk metadata?
Maria: attached smaps excerpt and runtime debug log (snippet): 
```
2026-03-16T09:12:43Z runtime: kv_alloc page addr=0x7f9b2a00000 len=2097152 pitch=65536 slot_count=32
2026-03-16T09:12:43Z runtime: kv_alloc page addr=0x7f9b2c00000 len=1048576 pitch=32768 slot_count=16
... repeated alternating pitches over time
```
Jonas: That alternating pitch smells like page stitching: kernel selection changed mid-run so the allocator mixes two page geometries. Leads to internal fragmentation and slower reuse.
Akash: We should try forcing a single kernel path for the whole run as an A/B. If that removes growth, it's a kernel-selection regression.
Maria: I ran that: forced kv-v2-compact on Hosted — memory stabilized, slight 2% latency degredation. Forcing kv-v1-std on Dedicated caused the Dedicated run to show the same growth.
Priya: That confirms it. Root cause = mixed kernel pitch + allocator alignment. Next: why does Hosted choose v1 more? Check driver capability detection and the fallback heuristics.
Theo: Could be the driver exposing a lower compute capability string with older driver. Also our capability table contains an override for "old-cu101" that forces v1. Might be mis-classifying some hosted nodes.
Akash: Ops: can you grep node labels? Maybe some hosted instances are still on cu101 image.
Maria: grep shows ~5% of hosted pool still running legacy image due to an image rollout abort. Those nodes end up in autoscaler. They have the fallback.
Jonas: Ops needs a rollout. In the meantime, we can make runtime pin page pitch at allocation time to avoid mixing: if current arena uses pitch P, allocate new pages with P. But that's a runtime change and needs test.
Priya: Also adding a small background compaction sweep (coalesce adjacent free slots of same pitch) could reclaim fragmentation without forcing kernel.
Theo: For VPC-specific note: VXLAN reassembly / smaller MTU increases page-copy count. Where we saw SG off stopping growth, that ties network path into the problem. Hosted VPCs with MTU 1400 more affected than Dedicated with 9000.
Akash: Action items: 
- Ops: finish hosted image rollout (priority) to remove misclassified nodes (Owner: Operations)
- Runtime: add opt-in pitch-pinning flag + compaction sweep (Owner: eng-runtime)
- Perf: run forced-kernel A/B across 3 long traces and capture jemalloc/smaps (Owner: Maria)
- Product: consider bumping hosted MTU recommendation in infra docs (Owner: Jonas)
Maria: I'll open a PR with the perf artifacts and a repro script (runs 12k tokens for 2h). Also adding a tiny script to detect mixed-pitch arenas at runtime and emit an alert.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline picked up maria/kv-pitch-fix branch — tests queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Akash: Nice. One more note — on on-prem (Private) installs, customers often use older kernels too; we should document that mixed-kernel allocation can manifest as slow memory growth, and include mitigation steps (force kernel path or runtime pin).
Priya: Agreed. I'll draft an internal doc with diagnostic commands: `pmap`, `cat /proc/<pid>/smaps | awk '/Private_/ {sum+= $2} END{print sum}'`, and runtime debug env VARs to enable page-pitch logging.
Maria: Thanks all. I'll follow up with PR link and perf numbers once tests finish. :thumbsup:
